Atomic bead claiming with per-workspace flock serialization.\n//!\n//! The Claimer wraps `BeadStore.claim()` with coordination that prevents\n//! thundering herd. A per-workspace flock serializes claim operations so\n//! workers take turns rather than racing on the same bead.\n//!\n//! Depends on: `types`, `bead_store`, `telemetry`.\n\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n\nuse anyhow::{anyhow, Result};\nuse fs2::FileExt;\n\nuse crate::bead_store::BeadStore;\nuse crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};\nuse crate::types::{Bead, BeadId, BeadStatus, ClaimOutcome, ClaimResult};\n\n/// Flock timeout: maximum time to wait for the workspace lock.\nconst FLOCK_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);\n\n/// Flock poll interval: time between lock acquisition attempts.\nconst FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);\n\n/// Number of consecutive claim errors before marking a bead suspect.\nconst CLAIM_ERROR_THRESHOLD: u32 = 3;\n\n/// Maximum claim-related history entries allowed before a bead is quarantined.\n///\n/// A single claim can append more than one history entry (for example,\n/// `claimed` plus `assignee_changed`), so this is intentionally a hard safety\n/// budget rather than a claim-attempt count.  The backend is checked before\n/// each mutation whenever it exposes event history.\nconst MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD: u32 = 100;\n\n/// Atomic bead claimer with workspace-level flock serialization.\npub struct Claimer {\n    store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,\n    lock_dir: PathBuf,\n    max_retries: u32,\n    retry_backoff_ms: u64,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n    /// Track consecutive claim errors per bead ID.\n    claim_errors: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<BeadId, u32>>>,\n    /// Track total claim events emitted per bead ID for circuit-breaking.\n    claim_events: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<BeadId, u32>>>,\n}\n\nimpl Claimer {\n    /// Create a new Claimer.\n    ///\n    /// - `store`: bead store for verify + claim operations\n    /// - `lock_dir`: directory for flock files (default: `/tmp`)\n    /// - `max_retries`: maximum claim attempts before giving up (default: 5)\n    /// - `retry_backoff_ms`: base backoff between retries in ms (default: 100)\n    /// - `telemetry`: telemetry emitter\n    pub fn new(\n        store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,\n        lock_dir: PathBuf,\n        max_retries: u32,\n        retry_backoff_ms: u64,\n        telemetry: Telemetry,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Claimer {\n            store,\n            lock_dir,\n            max_retries,\n            retry_backoff_ms,\n            telemetry,\n            claim_errors: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),\n            claim_events: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a claim error for a bead and check if the threshold is reached.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Some((consecutive_errors, last_error))` if the bead has reached\n    /// the error threshold, `None` otherwise. This is distinct from race-lost:\n    /// claim errors are CLI/store failures, not contention.\n    fn record_claim_error(&self, bead_id: &BeadId, error: &str) -> Option<(u32, String)> {\n        let mut errors = self.claim_errors.lock().unwrap();\n        let count = errors.entry(bead_id.clone()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        let consecutive = *count;\n        let last_error = error.to_string();\n\n        if consecutive >= CLAIM_ERROR_THRESHOLD {\n            // Reset the counter after reaching threshold so subsequent attempts\n            // start fresh (avoids emitting the same error repeatedly)\n            errors.remove(bead_id);\n            Some((consecutive, last_error))\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Clear claim errors for a bead (e.g., after a successful claim).\n    fn clear_claim_errors(&self, bead_id: &BeadId) {\n        let mut errors = self.claim_errors.lock().unwrap();\n        errors.remove(bead_id);\n    }\n\n    /// Check the in-memory fallback budget for backends that do not expose\n    /// claim history in their `show` projection.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Some(total_events)` after the budget is exhausted.\n    fn check_event_limit(&self, bead_id: &BeadId) -> Option<u32> {\n        let mut events = self.claim_events.lock().unwrap();\n        let count = events.entry(bead_id.clone()).or_insert(0);\n        *count += 1;\n        let total = *count;\n\n        if total > MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD {\n            Some(total)\n        } else {\n            None\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn trip_event_limit(&self, bead_id: &BeadId, event_count: u32) -> Result<String> {\n        let reason = format!(\n            \"claim history for bead {bead_id} reached {event_count} claim events (limit {MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD}); quarantining to prevent event-log runaway\"\n        );\n        if let Err(error) = self.store.block(bead_id).await {\n            let failure = format!(\"{reason}; quarantine failed: {error}\");\n            tracing::error!(%bead_id, %error, \"failed to quarantine bead after claim history limit\");\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                reason: failure.clone(),\n            })?;\n            return Err(anyhow!(failure));\n        }\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n            reason: reason.clone(),\n        })?;\n        Ok(reason)\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt to claim the next available bead from the candidate list.\n    ///\n    /// Iterates candidates in priority order, skipping those in the exclusion\n    /// set. For each candidate, acquires a per-workspace flock, verifies the\n    /// bead is still claimable, and attempts the claim.\n    ///\n    /// The `strand` parameter is the name of the strand that initiated the claim\n    /// (e.g., \"pluck\", \"mend\"). This is emitted in telemetry for the\n    /// `needle.beads.claimed` metric's `strand` attribute.\n    ///\n    /// Returns:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)`: successfully claimed a bead\n    /// - `AllRaceLost`: tried candidates, all race-lost\n    /// - `NoCandidates`: no candidates after filtering exclusions\n    /// - `StoreError(e)`: bead store or flock error\n    ///\n    /// NOTE: The caller is responsible for creating the `bead.claim` span\n    /// to ensure proper parent/child hierarchy (bead.claim should be a child\n    /// of bead.lifecycle, not strand.{name}).\n    pub async fn claim_next(\n        &self,\n        candidates: &[Bead],\n        actor: &str,\n        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n        strand: &str,\n    ) -> Result<ClaimOutcome> {\n        let eligible: Vec<&Bead> = candidates\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|b| !exclusions.contains(&b.id))\n            .collect();\n\n        if eligible.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(ClaimOutcome::NoCandidates);\n        }\n\n        let mut attempts = 0u32;\n\n        for candidate in &eligible {\n            if attempts >= self.max_retries {\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"max_retries_exceeded\");\n                // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", \"max_retries_exceeded\");\n                return Ok(ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost);\n            }\n\n            attempts += 1;\n            let bead_id = &candidate.id;\n\n            // Set bead_id and retry_number as span attributes.\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.bead.id\", bead_id.as_ref());\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.retry_number\", attempts);\n\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimAttempt {\n                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                attempt: attempts,\n            })?;\n\n            // Compute workspace lock path\n            let lock_path = workspace_lock_path(&self.lock_dir, &candidate.workspace);\n\n            // Acquire flock with timeout\n            let lock_file = match acquire_flock(&lock_path).await {\n                Ok(f) => f,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead_id, error = %e, \"flock timeout, skipping\");\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: format!(\"flock timeout: {e}\"),\n                    })?;\n                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current()\n                        .record(\"otel.status_description\", format!(\"flock timeout: {e}\"));\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));\n                }\n            };\n\n            // Verify bead is still claimable (status=open, no assignee)\n            let (current, claim_event_count) =\n                match self.store.show_with_claim_history(bead_id).await {\n                    Ok(b) => b,\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        drop(lock_file);\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                            reason: format!(\"verify failed: {e}\"),\n                        })?;\n                        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                        tracing::Span::current()\n                            .record(\"otel.status_description\", format!(\"verify failed: {e}\"));\n                        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));\n                    }\n                };\n\n            if current.status != BeadStatus::Open || current.assignee.is_some() {\n                drop(lock_file);\n                // Distinguish stale-assignee from race-lost: race_lost means another worker\n                // won the race (status changed), not that this bead has a leftover assignee.\n                if current.status == BeadStatus::Open && current.assignee.is_some() {\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: \"stale assignee\".to_string(),\n                    })?;\n                } else {\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLost {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                }\n                // Apply backoff before trying next candidate (same as store.claim RaceLost path)\n                if attempts < self.max_retries {\n                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(\n                        self.retry_backoff_ms * u64::from(attempts),\n                    ))\n                    .await;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            let in_memory_limit = if claim_event_count.is_none() {\n                self.check_event_limit(bead_id)\n            } else {\n                None\n            };\n            if let Some(event_count) = claim_event_count.or(in_memory_limit) {\n                if event_count >= MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD {\n                    drop(lock_file);\n                    let reason = self.trip_event_limit(bead_id, event_count).await?;\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        consecutive_errors: event_count,\n                        last_error: reason,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Attempt claim via store\n            let result = self.store.claim(bead_id, actor).await;\n            drop(lock_file);\n\n            match result {\n                Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead)) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"succeeded\");\n                    // Clear error counter on successful claim\n                    self.clear_claim_errors(bead_id);\n                    self.telemetry.set_workspace(bead.workspace.clone());\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        priority: candidate.priority as i32,\n                        strand: strand.to_string(),\n                    })?;\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Claimed(bead));\n                }\n                Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { .. }) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"race_lost\");\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLost {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    if attempts < self.max_retries {\n                        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(\n                            self.retry_backoff_ms * u64::from(attempts),\n                        ))\n                        .await;\n                    }\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason }) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Ok(ClaimResult::ClaimError { reason }) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    // Record claim error and check if threshold reached\n                    if let Some((consecutive, last_error)) =\n                        self.record_claim_error(bead_id, &reason)\n                    {\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimErrorThreshold {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,\n                            last_error: last_error.clone(),\n                        })?;\n                        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &last_error);\n                        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,\n                            last_error,\n                        });\n                    }\n                    // Continue to next candidate when threshold not yet reached\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Ok(ClaimResult::Suspect {\n                    bead_id: id,\n                    consecutive_errors,\n                    last_error,\n                }) => {\n                    // Bead is already marked suspect — propagate Suspect immediately\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %id,\n                        consecutive_errors,\n                        %last_error,\n                        \"bead already marked suspect, propagating without retry\"\n                    );\n                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\n                        \"otel.status_description\",\n                        format!(\n                            \"suspect: {} consecutive errors: {}\",\n                            consecutive_errors, last_error\n                        ),\n                    );\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {\n                        bead_id: id,\n                        consecutive_errors,\n                        last_error,\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    let reason = format!(\"store error: {e}\");\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    // Record claim error and check if threshold reached\n                    if let Some((consecutive, last_error)) =\n                        self.record_claim_error(bead_id, &reason)\n                    {\n                        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimErrorThreshold {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,\n                            last_error: last_error.clone(),\n                        })?;\n                        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &last_error);\n                        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Suspect {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                            consecutive_errors: consecutive,\n                            last_error,\n                        });\n                    }\n                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", reason);\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Exhausted all eligible candidates without success\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"all_race_lost\");\n        // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", \"all_race_lost\");\n        Ok(ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost)\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience: claim a single bead by ID (fetches the bead, then delegates\n    /// to `claim_next` with a single-element candidate list).\n    ///\n    /// The `exclusions` parameter allows the caller to pass beads that should\n    /// be skipped (e.g., beads that recently lost a claim race). This prevents\n    /// tight loops when multiple workers are racing on the same bead.\n    ///\n    /// The `strand` parameter is optional; if not provided, defaults to \"unknown\".\n    pub async fn claim_one(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &BeadId,\n        actor: &str,\n        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n        strand: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        let bead = self.store.show(bead_id).await?;\n\n        // If the bead is in the exclusion set, return NotClaimable immediately\n        // without attempting the claim. This prevents tight loops when the worker\n        // has already lost a race on this bead.\n        if exclusions.contains(bead_id) {\n            return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"bead is excluded\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        match self\n            .claim_next(&[bead], actor, exclusions, strand.unwrap_or(\"unknown\"))\n            .await?\n        {\n            ClaimOutcome::Claimed(b) => Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(b)),\n            ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost => Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost {\n                claimed_by: \"(race)\".to_string(),\n            }),\n            ClaimOutcome::NoCandidates => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no candidates\".to_string(),\n            }),\n            ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e) => Err(e),\n            ClaimOutcome::Suspect {\n                bead_id,\n                consecutive_errors,\n                last_error,\n            } => Ok(ClaimResult::Suspect {\n                bead_id,\n                consecutive_errors,\n                last_error,\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Atomically claim the next available bead using server-side selection.\n    ///\n    /// This is the preferred method for multi-worker scenarios. It calls\n    /// `BeadStore::claim_auto()` which atomically finds and claims a bead in\n    /// a single transaction, guaranteeing that concurrent workers receive\n    /// distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// The `strand` parameter is the name of the strand that initiated the claim\n    /// (e.g., \"pluck\", \"mend\"). This is emitted in telemetry for the\n    /// `needle.beads.claimed` metric's `strand` attribute.\n    ///\n    /// Returns:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)`: successfully claimed a bead\n    /// - `NotClaimable(reason)`: no beads available to claim\n    /// - `StoreError(e)`: bead store error\n    pub async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str, strand: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimAttempt {\n            bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n            attempt: 1,\n        })?;\n\n        match self.store.claim_auto(actor).await {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead)) => {\n                let claim_event_count = match self.store.show_with_claim_history(&bead.id).await {\n                    Ok((_, count)) => count,\n                    Err(error) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            %error,\n                            \"unable to inspect claim history after atomic claim\"\n                        );\n                        None\n                    }\n                };\n                let in_memory_count = if claim_event_count.is_none() {\n                    Some(self.check_event_limit(&bead.id).unwrap_or(0))\n                } else {\n                    None\n                };\n                let event_count = claim_event_count.or(in_memory_count).unwrap_or(0);\n                if event_count >= MAX_CLAIM_EVENTS_PER_BEAD {\n                    let reason = self.trip_event_limit(&bead.id, event_count).await?;\n                    return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason });\n                }\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.bead.id\", bead.id.as_ref());\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"succeeded\");\n                self.telemetry.set_workspace(bead.workspace.clone());\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    priority: bead.priority as i32,\n                    strand: strand.to_string(),\n                })?;\n                Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n            }\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason }) => {\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                    bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason })\n            }\n            Ok(other) => {\n                // RaceLost shouldn't happen with claim_auto, but handle it\n                tracing::warn!(?other, \"claim_auto returned unexpected result\");\n                Ok(other)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                let reason = format!(\"store error: {e}\");\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &reason);\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                    bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Err(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a deterministic lock file path for a workspace.\n///\n/// Uses a simple hash (not crypto) of the workspace path. All workers\n/// compute the same hash for the same workspace.\nfn workspace_lock_path(lock_dir: &Path, workspace: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\n    workspace.hash(&mut hasher);\n    let hash = hasher.finish();\n    lock_dir.join(format!(\"needle-claim-{:016x}.lock\", hash))\n}\n\n/// Acquire an exclusive flock with a 10-second timeout.\n///\n/// Returns the locked file on success. The lock is released when the\n/// file is dropped (flock auto-releases on close).\npub async fn acquire_flock(lock_path: &Path) -> Result<std::fs::File> {\n    if let Some(parent) = lock_path.parent() {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;\n    }\n\n    let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .truncate(false)\n        .write(true)\n        .open(lock_path)?;\n\n    let deadline = Instant::now() + FLOCK_TIMEOUT;\n    loop {\n        match file.try_lock_exclusive() {\n            Ok(()) => return Ok(file),\n            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                if Instant::now() >= deadline {\n                    return Err(anyhow!(\n                        \"flock timeout after {}s on {}\",\n                        FLOCK_TIMEOUT.as_secs(),\n                        lock_path.display()\n                    ));\n                }\n                tokio::time::sleep(FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_4df31ffe44ea47cfbc2f9e79","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Span-Scope Preservation Pattern Design\n2\t\n3\t## Problem Statement\n4\t\n5\tThe current NEEDLE worker uses `tracing::Span` for telemetry hierarchy with `in_scope()` for synchronous code sections. This creates LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) violations when multiple claim cycles run concurrently across different execution contexts, causing scope leakage where telemetry from one bead's lifecycle bleeds into another's.\n6\t\n7\t**Root Cause:** `EnteredSpan` guards mutate a thread-local stack and cannot safely be stored across `.await` points. The current workaround stores `Span` directly and uses `in_scope()`, but this is not LIFO-safe in async contexts with concurrent claim cycles.\n8\t\n9\t## Current State Analysis\n10\t\n11\t### Existing Pattern\n12\t```rust\n13\t// Worker stores lifecycle span as Span (not EnteredSpan)\n14\tbead_lifecycle_span: Option<tracing::Span>\n15\t\n16\t// Usage in state machine:\n17\tlifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?\n18\tdo_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\t### Telemetry Attributes to Preserve\n22\t```rust\n23\tneedle.bead.id = %bead_id\n24\tneedle.bead.priority = %priority\n25\tneedle.bead.title_hash = %title_hash\n26\tneedle.bead.outcome = %outcome  // Set on completion\n27\t```\n28\t\n29\t### Current Span Hierarchy\n30\t```\n31\tworker.session (root)\n32\t└── strand.pluck\n33\t    └── bead.lifecycle              ← Stored across .await\n34\t        ├── bead.claim             (ATOMIC phase)\n35\t        ├── bead.prompt_build\n36\t        ├── agent.dispatch\n37\t        │   └── agent.execution\n38\t        └── bead.outcome\n39\t            └── bead.mitosis?\n40\t```\n41\t\n42\t## Design Decision: ScopeGuard Pattern with Explicit Instrumentation\n43\t\n44\t**Chosen Approach:** Replace `in_scope()` with a `ScopeGuard` that uses explicit `.instrument()` on futures and a RAII guard for synchronous sections, ensuring LIFO-compliant scope management.\n45\t\n46\t### Why This Pattern\n47\t\n48\t1. **LIFO Compliance:** ScopeGuard explicitly unwinds in reverse order on drop\n49\t2. **Async Safety:** No thread-local mutations across `.await` points\n50\t3. **Attribute Preservation:** Span attributes are captured at creation time\n51\t4. **Zero Overhead:** Compile-time guard with runtime cost equal to current approach\n52\t5. **Ergonomics:** Drop-in replacement for `in_scope()` with minimal code changes\n53\t\n54\t### Rejected Alternatives\n55\t\n56\t1. **Span with in_scope():** Current approach - not LIFO-safe, causes scope leakage\n57\t2. **EnteredSpan storage:** Violates thread-local safety across `.await`\n58\t3. **Manual span enter/exit:** Error-prone, easy to forget cleanup\n59\t4. **Async scope guards:** Requires runtime support, adds overhead\n60\t\n61\t## Proposed API\n62\t\n63\t### Core Type: ScopeGuard\n64\t\n65\t```rust\n66\t/// RAII guard for LIFO-safe span scoping.\n67\t///\n68\t/// When dropped, the span is explicitly closed, ensuring proper unwinding\n69\t/// even across early returns or errors.\n70\tpub struct ScopeGuard {\n71\t    span: Span,\n72\t    _guard: Option<tracing::span::EnteredSpan>,\n73\t}\n74\t\n75\timpl ScopeGuard {\n76\t    /// Create a new scope guard from a span, entering it immediately.\n77\t    ///\n78\t    /// The span will be exited when the guard is dropped (LIFO order).\n79\t    pub fn new(span: Span) -> Self {\n80\t        let _guard = Some(span.enter());\n81\t        Self { span, _guard }\n82\t    }\n83\t\n84\t    /// Enter the span scope for a synchronous block.\n85\t    ///\n86\t    /// Prefer `ScopeGuard::new()` over this method for automatic cleanup.\n87\t    /// This method exists for cases where manual scope control is needed.\n88\t    pub fn enter_scope(&self, f: impl FnOnce()) {\n89\t        let _guard = self.span.enter();\n90\t        f();\n91\t    }\n92\t\n93\t    /// Record an attribute on the span.\n94\t    pub fn record(&self, key: &str, value: impl tracing::Value) {\n95\t        self.span.record(key, value);\n96\t    }\n97\t}\n98\t\n99\timpl Drop for ScopeGuard {\n100\t    fn drop(&mut self) {\n101\t        // Explicit cleanup - _guard drop handles the actual exit\n102\t        self._guard.take();\n103\t    }\n104\t}\n105\t```\n106\t\n107\t### Usage Examples\n108\t\n109\t#### Before (Current Pattern - LIFO-unsafe)\n110\t```rust\n111\tlifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?\n112\t```\n113\t\n114\t#### After (ScopeGuard Pattern - LIFO-safe)\n115\t```rust\n116\t// Option 1: Direct guard (preferred)\n117\tlet _guard = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_span.clone());\n118\tself.do_log()?;\n119\t\n120\t// Option 2: Explicit scope\n121\tlifecycle_guard.enter_scope(|| self.do_log())?;\n122\t```\n123\t\n124\t#### Async Context (No Change Needed)\n125\t```rust\n126\t// Already safe - instrument() doesn't mutate thread-local\n127\tdo_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await\n128\t```\n129\t\n130\t## Implementation Strategy\n131\t\n132\t### Phase 1: Core Infrastructure\n133\t1. Add `ScopeGuard` type to `src/span/mod.rs`\n134\t2. Add unit tests for LIFO compliance\n135\t3. Add integration test with concurrent claim cycles\n136\t\n137\t### Phase 2: Worker Migration\n138\t1. Replace `lifecycle_span.in_scope()` calls in `worker/mod.rs`\n139\t2. Verify no `EnteredSpan` is stored across `.await`\n140\t3. Add compile-time assertions for span type safety\n141\t\n142\t### Phase 3: Validation\n143\t1. Run integration tests with concurrent workers\n144\t2. Verify telemetry attributes preserved across all span types\n145\t3. Check for scope leakage in logs\n146\t\n147\t## Telemetry Field Preservation\n148\t\n149\t### Span Creation (Current - Preserved)\n150\t```rust\n151\tlet lifecycle_span = tracing::info_span!(\n152\t    \"bead.lifecycle\",\n153\t    needle.bead.id = %bead_id,\n154\t    needle.bead.priority = %priority,\n155\t    needle.bead.title_hash = %title_hash,\n156\t    needle.bead.outcome = tracing::field::Empty,  // Set later\n157\t);\n158\t```\n159\t\n160\t### Attribute Updates (New API)\n161\t```rust\n162\t// Instead of: lifecycle_span.record(\"needle.bead.outcome\", outcome)\n163\tlifecycle_guard.record(\"needle.bead.outcome\", outcome);\n164\t```\n165\t\n166\t### Verification Checklist\n167\t- [ ] `needle.bead.id` captured at span creation\n168\t- [ ] `needle.bead.priority` captured at span creation\n169\t- [ ] `needle.bead.title_hash` captured at span creation\n170\t- [ ] `needle.bead.outcome` set on completion (via ScopeGuard::record)\n171\t- [ ] All fields present in exported OTLP traces\n172\t- [ ] No field loss during scope transitions\n173\t\n174\t## Scope Unwinding Strategy\n175\t\n176\t### LIFO Compliance\n177\t\n178\tThe `ScopeGuard` ensures LIFO unwinding through RAII:\n179\t\n180\t```rust\n181\t// Multiple scopes nest correctly (LIFO)\n182\tlet _outer = ScopeGuard::new(outer_span);\n183\t{\n184\t    let _inner = ScopeGuard::new(inner_span);\n185\t    // do_work() - inner span active\n186\t} // inner span dropped here (correct LIFO)\n187\t// outer span still active\n188\t```\n189\t\n190\t### Multiple Claim Cycles\n191\t\n192\tWhen a worker completes a bead and claims another:\n193\t\n194\t```rust\n195\t// Cycle 1: Claim and process bead A\n196\tlet lifecycle_a = create_lifecycle_span(&bead_a);\n197\tlet _guard_a = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_a);\n198\tprocess_bead_a().await;\n199\t// _guard_a dropped here - span A closed\n200\t\n201\t// Cycle 2: Claim and process bead B\n202\tlet lifecycle_b = create_lifecycle_span(&bead_b);\n203\tlet _guard_b = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_b);\n204\tprocess_bead().await;\n205\t// No leakage from A to B\n206\t```\n207\t\n208\t### Async Context Safety\n209\t\n210\t```rust\n211\t// Safe: No guard across .await\n212\tlet lifecycle_span = self.bead_lifecycle_span.clone().unwrap();\n213\tdo_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span).await?;\n214\t\n215\t// Unsafe: Guard stored across .await (CATCH THIS IN CODE REVIEW)\n216\tlet guard = ScopeGuard::new(span); // ❌ NEVER DO THIS\n217\tlong_async_operation().await; // UB - guard dropped after await\n218\t```\n219\t\n220\t## Before/After Transformation\n221\t\n222\t### Example 1: do_log() call\n223\t\n224\t**Before:**\n225\t```rust\n226\tWorkerState::Logging => lifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?,\n227\t```\n228\t\n229\t**After:**\n230\t```rust\n231\tWorkerState::Logging => {\n232\t    let _guard = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_span.clone());\n233\t    self.do_log()\n234\t}?,\n235\t```\n236\t\n237\t### Example 2: Multiple nested scopes\n238\t\n239\t**Before:**\n240\t```rust\n241\touter_span.in_scope(|| {\n242\t    inner_span.in_scope(|| {\n243\t        do_work()\n244\t    })\n245\t})\n246\t```\n247\t\n248\t**After:**\n249\t```rust\n250\tlet _outer = ScopeGuard::new(outer_span.clone());\n251\t{\n252\t    let _inner = ScopeGuard::new(inner_span.clone());\n253\t    do_work()\n254\t} // inner closed\n255\t// outer still active\n256\t```\n257\t\n258\t### Example 3: State machine with multiple self.do_dispatch().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?;\n275\t    self.do_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?;\n276\t},\n277\tWorkerState::Logging => {\n278\t    let _guard = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_span.clone());\n279\t    self.do_log()\n280\t}?,\n281\t```\n282\t\n283\t## Testing Strategy\n284\t\n285\t### Unit Tests\n286\t\n287\t```rust\n288\t#[cfg(test)]\n289\tmod tests {\n290\t    use super::*;\n291\t\n292\t    #[test]\n293\t    fn test_scope_guard_lifo_unwinding() {\n294\t        let outer = tracing::info_span!(\"outer\");\n295\t        let inner = tracing::info_span!(\"inner\", parent = &outer);\n296\t\n297\t        let _outer_guard = ScopeGuard::new(outer);\n298\t        {\n299\t            let _inner_guard = ScopeGuard::new(inner);\n300\t            // Inner span should be current\n301\t            assert!(span_is_current(&inner));\n302\t        }\n303\t        // Outer span should be current after inner dropped\n304\t        assert!(span_is_current(&outer));\n305\t    }\n306\t\n307\t    #[test]\n308\t    fn test_attribute_preservation() {\n309\t        let span = tracing::info_span!(\n310\t            \"test\",\n311\t This creates LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) violations when multiple claim cycles run concurrently across different execution contexts, causing scope leakage where telemetry from one bead's lifecycle bleeds into another's.\n\n**Root Cause:** `EnteredSpan` guards mutate a thread-local stack and cannot safely be stored across `.await` points. The current workaround stores `Span` directly and uses `in_scope()`, but this is not LIFO-safe in async contexts with concurrent claim cycles.\n\n## Current State Analysis\n\n### Existing Pattern\n```rust\n// Worker stores lifecycle span as Span (not EnteredSpan)\nbead_lifecycle_span: Option<tracing::Span>\n\n// Usage in state machine:\nlifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?\ndo_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await\n```\n\n### Telemetry Attributes to Preserve\n```rust\nneedle.bead.id = %bead_id\nneedle.bead.priority = %priority\nneedle.bead.title_hash = %title_hash\nneedle.bead.outcome = %outcome  // Set on completion\n```\n\n### Current Span Hierarchy\n```\nworker.session (root)\n└── strand.pluck\n    └── bead.lifecycle              ← Stored across .await\n        ├── bead.claim             (ATOMIC phase)\n        ├── bead.prompt_build\n        ├── agent.dispatch\n        │   └── agent.execution\n        └── bead.outcome\n            └── bead.mitosis?\n```\n\n## Design Decision: ScopeGuard Pattern with Explicit Instrumentation\n\n**Chosen Approach:** Replace `in_scope()` with a `ScopeGuard` that uses explicit `.instrument()` on futures and a RAII guard for synchronous sections, ensuring LIFO-compliant scope management.\n\n### Why This Pattern\n\n1. **LIFO Compliance:** ScopeGuard explicitly unwinds in reverse order on drop\n2. **Async Safety:** No thread-local mutations across `.await` points\n3. **Attribute Preservation:** Span attributes are captured at creation time\n4. **Zero Overhead:** Compile-time guard with runtime cost equal to current approach\n5. **Ergonomics:** Drop-in replacement for `in_scope()` with minimal code changes\n\n### Rejected Alternatives\n\n1. **Span with in_scope():** Current approach - not LIFO-safe, causes scope leakage\n2. **EnteredSpan storage:** Violates thread-local safety across `.await`\n3. **Manual span enter/exit:** Error-prone, easy to forget cleanup\n4. **Async scope guards:** Requires runtime support, adds overhead\n\n## Proposed API\n\n### Core Type: ScopeGuard\n\n```rust\n/// RAII guard for LIFO-safe span scoping.\n///\n/// When dropped, the span is explicitly closed, ensuring proper unwinding\n/// even across early returns or errors.\npub struct ScopeGuard {\n    span: Span,\n    _guard: Option<tracing::span::EnteredSpan>,\n}\n\nimpl ScopeGuard {\n    /// Create a new scope guard from a span, entering it immediately.\n    ///\n    /// The span will be exited when the guard is dropped (LIFO order).\n    pub fn new(span: Span) -> Self {\n        let _guard = Some(span.enter());\n        Self { span, _guard }\n    }\n\n    /// Enter the span scope for a synchronous block.\n    ///\n    /// Prefer `ScopeGuard::new()` over this method for automatic cleanup.\n    /// This method exists for cases where manual scope control is needed.\n    pub fn enter_scope(&self, f: impl FnOnce()) {\n        let _guard = self.span.enter();\n        f();\n    }\n\n    /// Record an attribute on the span.\n    pub fn record(&self, key: &str, value: impl tracing::Value) {\n        self.span.record(key, value);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ScopeGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        // Explicit cleanup - _guard drop handles the actual exit\n        self._guard.take();\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Usage Examples\n\n#### Before (Current Pattern - LIFO-unsafe)\n```rust\nlifecycle_span.in_scope(|| self.do_log())?\n```\n\n#### After (ScopeGuard Pattern - LIFO-safe)\n```rust\n// Option 1: Direct guard (preferred)\nlet _guard = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_span.clone());\nself.do_log()?;\n\n// Option 2: Explicit scope\nlifecycle_guard.enter_scope(|| self.do_log())?;\n```\n\n#### Async Context (No Change Needed)\n```rust\n// Already safe - instrument() doesn't mutate thread-local\ndo_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await\n```\n\n## Implementation Strategy\n\n### Phase 1: Core Infrastructure\n1. Run integration tests with concurrent workers\n2. Verify telemetry attributes preserved across all span types\n3. Check for scope leakage in logs\n\n## Telemetry Field Preservation\n\n### Span Creation (Current - Preserved)\n```rust\nlet lifecycle_span = tracing::info_span!(\n    \"bead.lifecycle\",\n    needle.bead.id = %bead_id,\n    needle.bead.priority = %priority,\n    needle.bead.title_hash = %title_hash,\n    needle.bead.outcome = tracing::field::Empty,  // Set later\n);\n```\n\n### Attribute Updates (New API)\n```rust\n// Instead of: lifecycle_span.record(\"needle.bead.outcome\", outcome)\nlifecycle_guard.record(\"needle.bead.outcome\", outcome);\n```\n\n### Verification Checklist\n- [ ] `needle.bead.id` captured at span creation\n- [ ] `needle.bead.priority` captured at span creation\n- [ ] `needle.bead.title_hash` captured at span creation\n- [ ] `needle.bead.outcome` set on completion (via ScopeGuard::record)\n- [ ] All fields present in exported OTLP traces\n- [ ] No field loss during scope transitions\n\n## Scope Unwinding Strategy\n\n### LIFO Compliance\n\nThe `ScopeGuard` ensures LIFO unwinding through RAII:\n\n```rust\n// Multiple scopes nest correctly (LIFO)\nlet _outer = ScopeGuard::new(outer_span);\n{\n    let _inner = ScopeGuard::new(inner_span);\n    // do_work() - inner span active\n} // inner span dropped here (correct LIFO)\n// outer span still active\n```\n\n### Multiple Claim Cycles\n\nWhen a worker completes a bead and claims another:\n\n```rust\n// Cycle 1: Claim and process bead A\nlet lifecycle_a = create_lifecycle_span(&bead_a);\nlet _guard_a = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_a);\nprocess_bead_a().await;\n// _guard_a dropped here - span A closed\n\n// Cycle 2: Claim and process bead B\nlet lifecycle_b = create_lifecycle_span(&bead_b);\nlet _guard_b = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_b);\nprocess_bead().await;\n// No leakage from A to B\n```\n\n### Async Context Safety\n\n```rust\n// Safe: No guard across .await\nlet lifecycle_span = ScopeGuard::new(lifecycle_span.clone());\n    self.do_log()\n}?,\n```\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Tests\n\n```rust\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn guards)\n61\tself.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span);\n62\t\n63\t// Instrument subsequent operations\n64\tself.do_build().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?;\n65\tself.do_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?;\n66\t```\n67\t\n68\t### Pros\n69\t\n70\t- ✅ **LIFO safe**: No entered guards, no thread-local stack manipulation\n71\t- ✅ **Async compatible**: Spans stored as plain values, safe across `.await`\n72\t- ✅ **Telemetry preserved**: All fields recordable via `.record()` before instrumentation\n73\t- ✅ **Concurrent-safe**: Each future gets its own span attachment, no shared mutable state\n74\t- ✅ **Tested in production**: Current NEEDLE implementation, proven stable post-bf-3uj6i\n75\t- ✅ **Explicit lifecycle**: Span attachment clear from code structure\n76\t- ✅ **Composable**: Can instrument nested futures with different spans\n77\t\n78\t### Cons\n79\t\n80\t- ❌ **Span per-future overhead**: Each instrumented call clones the span\n81\t- ❌ **Manual propagation**: Must remember to `.instrument()` every call\n82\t- ❌ **No automatic context**: Cannot span `.await` boundaries without breaking LIFO. Would require splitting every async operation into pre/post sync blocks.\n\n### Telemetry Preservation\n\n**GOOD for sync, BROKEN for async** - Sync blocks preserve telemetry. Async work would lose span context at `.await` boundaries.\n\n### Concurrent Claim Cycle Support\n\n**GOOD** - Each operation has its own span, no shared state. However, the pattern's async limitations make it impractical for NEEDLE's state machine.\n\n---\n\n## Pattern 3: Thread-Local Span Stack with Async-Aware Guards (Experimental)\n\n### Description\n\nA custom span guard that detects thread migration and safely handles span stack restoration. This is a theoretical pattern not present in the current `tracing` crate but could be implemented.\n\n```rust\nstruct AsyncSpanGuard {\n    span: tracing::Span,\n    original_thread_id: ThreadId,\n}\n\nimpl AsyncSpanGuard {\n    fn new(span: tracing::Span) -> Self {\n        let thread_id = std::thread::current().id();\n        span.enter();\n        Self { span, original_thread_id: thread_id }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for AsyncSpanGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let current_thread = std::thread::current().id();\n        if current_thread == self.original_thread_id {\n            // Safe to exit normally\n            self.span.exit();\n        } else {\n            // Thread migration occurred - span already orphaned\n            // Would need runtime to track and clean up orphaned spans\n            // This is the hard part: no API to remove from specific thread's stack\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Pros\n\n- ✅ **Familiar API**: RAII guard pattern matches user expectations\n- ✅ **Automatic context**: All code in scope sees the span\n- ✅ **Less verbose**: No manual instrumentation at each call site\n\n### Cons\n\n- ❌ **Not currently feasible**: `tracing` crate provides no API to manipulate other threads' span stacks\n- ❌ **Requires runtime changes**: Would need tracing-span-level coordination or custom subscriber\n- ❌ **Complex implementation**: Tracking orphaned spans across threads is non-trivial\n- ❌ **Performance overhead**: Thread ID checks on every drop, potential contention\n- ❌ **Unproven**: No production examples of this pattern in the wild\n\n### LIFO Safety Analysis\n\n**THEORETICAL** - Would require deep runtime support. The `tracing` crate's subscriber model assumes per-thread span stacks with no cross-thread manipulation APIs. Implementing this would likely require a custom subscriber with inter-thread coordination.\n\n### Async Compatibility\n\n**POTENTIALLY FULL** - If implemented correctly, guards could be held across `.await`. But the implementation complexity is extremely high.\n\n### Telemetry Preservation\n\n**FULL** - Same as normal guards when on the same thread. Cross-thread behavior depends on implementation.\n\n### Concurrent Claim Cycle Support\n\n**UNKNOWN** - Depends on implementation. Could have performance implications from thread coordination.\n\n---\n\n## Pattern Recommendation\n\n### **Winner: Pattern 1 (Span with `.instrument()`)**\n\n**Justification:**\n\n1. **Proven in production**: Current NEEDLE implementation uses this pattern successfully post-bf-3uj6i\n2. **Zero LIFO violations**: No entered guards means no thread-local stack manipulation\n3. **Full async compatibility**: Spans are plain data, safe across thread boundaries\n4. **Good concurrent support**: Each operation has independent span instances\n5. **Maintainable**: Clear, explicit pattern that's easy to audit\n\n**Pattern 2 (`in_scope()`)** is safe only for synchronous code and breaks NEEDLE's async state machine flow.\n\n**Pattern 3 (Async-Aware Guards)** is theoretically interesting but not practically feasible without major changes to the `tracing` crate's subscriber model.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Guidance for NEEDLE\n\n### Current Best Practices (Already in Use)\n\n```rust\n// ✅ CORRECT: Create span, instrument future\nlet dispatch_span = tracing::info_span!(\n    \"agent.dispatch\",\n    needle.bead.id = %bead_id.as_ref(),\n    needle.agent.pid = tracing::field::Empty,\n);\nlet result = self.run_process(...).instrument(dispatch_span).await?;\n\n// ✅ CORRECT: Store span for later instrumentation\nself.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span);\n\n// ✅ CORRECT: Instrument each state transition\nself.do_build().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?;\nself.do_execute().instrument(lifecycle_span.clone()).await?;\n\n// ❌ WRONG: Never do this\n// let _guard = lifecycle_span.enter();  // Violates LIFO across await\n// self.do_execute().await?;            // Task may resume on different thread\n```\n\n### Struct Field Documentation\n\nAll span fields MUST be documented:\n\n```rust\n/// The current bead lifecycle span. Created when a bead is claimed and\n/// instrumented onto each state-handler future until the lifecycle ends.\n///\n/// **This must remain a `Span`, not an `EnteredSpan`**: entered guards mutate a\n/// thread-local stack and cannot safely be stored across `.await` points.\nbead_lifecycle_span: Option<tracing::Span>,\n```\n\n### Defensive Measures\n\n- **Line length limits**: `log_writer.rs` caps line length at 10K chars to bound damage from span leaks\n- **Explicit comments**: Multiple code comments reference bf-3uj6i to prevent regression\n- **Testing**: Run workers under load to verify no span stack growth occurs\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nPattern 1 (Span with `.instrument()`) is the only pattern that simultaneously guarantees LIFO safety, full async compatibility, and proper telemetry preservation for NEEDLE's concurrent claim cycle workload.
